chunks: Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, may Allah have mercy on him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I heard al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام informing a man of his own death. So I said to myself, “Indeed, he knows when a man from his Shiʿah will die.” Then he turned toward me somewhat angrily and said: “O Isḥāq, Rushayd al-Hajarī used to know the knowledge of deaths and afflictions, and the Imam is worthier of the knowledge of that.”

Then he said: “O Isḥāq, do whatever you are doing, for your lifespan has come to an end, and you will die within two years. Your brothers and the people of your household will not remain after you except a little while, until their unity is broken apart and some of them betray others, until their enemy gloats over them. So this was what was within yourself?”

So I said: “Then I seek the forgiveness of Allah for what occurred in my breast.” Isḥāq did not remain after this gathering except a short while until he died. Then only a little time passed over them before Banū ʿAmmār rose with the wealth of the people, and they became bankrupt.

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the divinely designated Imam possessing higher authority and knowledge
key_terms.الْعَبْدَ الصَّالِحَ: a title referring to Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام
key_terms.بِأَمْوَالِ النَّاسِ: with the wealth of the people, meaning their property and funds
key_terms.شِيعَتِهِ: his followers and adherents among the Shiʿah
key_terms.عُمُرَكَ: your lifespan or allotted term of life
key_terms.عِلْمَ الْمَنَايَا: knowledge of appointed deaths and times of dying

ai.seo_question: How does al-Kāfī describe the Imam’s knowledge of deaths and future afflictions?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts how Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام informed Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār of his approaching death and the later disintegration of his family’s affairs. It highlights the divinely granted knowledge of the Imam regarding deaths and afflictions, and records the subsequent fulfillment of what the Imam عليه السلام foretold.
